messages.text: Hrgovic: Itauma is ‘amazing’ but boxed like an ‘amateur’

metadata.summary: Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”.
metadata.content: Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Filip Hrgovic: Moses Itauma 'amazing' but boxed 'like an amateur' in thrilling heavyweight fight at The O2 Filip Hrgovic secured one of the biggest shocks in boxing this year after stopping an exhausted Moses Itauma in the ninth round at The O2; Hrgovic becomes Croatia's first-ever world heavyweight champion By David Rivers Sunday 30 August 2026 08:51, UK Image: Filip Hrgovic lands a punch on Moses Itauma (left) during his win Filip Hrgovic praised Moses Itauma after his shock ninth-round stoppage but said his opponent had boxed “like an amateur”. Hrgovic became Croatia's first world heavyweight champion at The O2 on Saturday night to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Itauma, who was unbeaten coming into the bout, was dominant in the first six rounds after landing a string of accurate blows. But he became visibly exhausted as the fight progressed and he failed to find a way past Hrgovic's durable chin, with the seventh round being the first time in his career he had been past six rounds. metadata.summary: Ruoning Yin produced a final-hole chip-in to take a one-shot lead into the final round of the LPGA Tour’s FM Championship, as European title hopes faded in Boston.
metadata.content: LPGA Tour: Ruoning Yin grabs FM Championship lead after late chip-in as European title challenge fades in Boston | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to content LPGA Tour: Ruoning Yin grabs FM Championship lead after late chip-in as European title challenge fades in Boston The LPGA Tour's FM Championship and the Ladies European Tour's KPMG Women's PGA Championship are the last events before Team Europe look to regain the Solheim Cup against Team USA, live from September 11-13 on Sky Sports Golf; Sunday 30 August 2026 07:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ruoning Yin’s chip in sees her take a one-shot lead at the FM Championship in Massachusetts. Ruoning Yin produced a final-hole chip-in to take a one-shot lead into the final round of the LPGA Tour’s FM Championship, as European title hopes faded in Boston. Yin holed her chip from just off the 18th green, having also posted a 20-foot birdie on the par-three 16th, to close a four-under 68 and move to 12 under at TPC Boston. The five-time LPGA Tour winner holds a slender lead over South Korean duo Sei Young Kim and Hyo Joo Kim, with Somi Lee a further three strokes back alongside American Jenny Bae.
